title: How Jacky Chou's income fell from $500k/mo to $200k/mo: revenue-source breakdown and the sprint-on-winners rule
summary: Jacky compares his revenue sources from a year ago (about $506k/mo) to the current month (about $200k/mo) after a Google hit. He explains the Partnerships/domain-rental push that built the peak, then gives his rules for repeating success: keep testing, don't trust SEO philosophers, and sprint all-in when something works.

principles.text: Don't trust others' claims about what works in SEO; run your own tests properly.
principles.quote: do not take anyone's word for things like oh this works this doesn't cuz most of these guys are just like SEO philosophers when you do a test you have to you run it properly

principles.text: Always be testing; replicating big revenue comes from continuous experimentation.
principles.quote: you have to be always testing right

principles.text: When a test hits, drop everything and sprint at it with the whole team; the rest of the time you can walk.
principles.quote: once something hits you have to push super hard it's kind of like a Sprint like you're kind of walking the whole time kind of checking out you know smelling the flowers and all that but when when something hits

principles.text: If you find something working, cancel other plans and go all in, even on a weekend.
principles.quote: if I found something that's working on Saturday morning bro I'm canceling all my all my uh plans that weekend we we're doing this all in my whole team is dedicated to this right now

principles.text: Set yourself up to monetize luck: luck exists, but preparation lets you capture it.
principles.quote: there's some luck but like you have to kind of set yourself up to mon ize that luck

principles.text: His peak came from leveraging other people's domains via partnerships and pushing it relentlessly with a large team.
principles.quote: I identified the power of Partnerships leveraging like other people's domains and I kept pushing it you guys don't you you wouldn't believe how hard I pushed it
